top_signals.title: The U.S. Has $50 Billion for Nuclear Waste and Nowhere to Put It
top_signals.summary: Finland and the United States are exemplifying two opposing approaches to managing the mounting problem of spent nuclear fuel. Finland is about to open the world’s first permanent nuclear waste disposal facility. The United States is stuck in a cycle of endless political turnover and resultant gridlock about how to address the more than 90,000 metric tons of spent fuel sitting in temporary facilities around the country, posing a mounting public health hazard and tax dollar sink.  The Onkalo site (named after the Finnish for ‘cave’)…
